newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs trade $0.50 lower-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs trade $0.50 lower-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Wednesday sold $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by falling pork prices and adequate hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold at $46.50 to $47.50 in the country and at plants, $48.00 to $48.50. At least one major packer said it had enough hogs bought for Wednesday slaughter.
Illinois hogs sold at $46.50 to $47.50 in the country and $48.00 to $48.50 at the plant.
Indiana hogs sold $47.00 to $47.50 in the country and $48.00 to $48.50 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold at $46.50 to $47.50 in the country and $48.50 to $49.50 at plants.
Weak pork demand was tied to ideas retailers had the hams needed for Easter promotions late in the month.

Pork cutout values on Tuesday were quoted down $0.28 to $0.30 per cwt, USDA said. Fresh pork loin prices were weak to $1.00 per cwt lower than Monday, hams ranged steady to $2.00 lower and pork bellies were steady, USDA said.
Cash hog price declines also were attributed to sufficient hog marketings, although reduced movement at some local points could limit cash weakness, dealers said.
